title: Ember Vault mapping
description: How Ember Vault reads another tool's JSON or YAML. Put it in your content folder's Importers folder.

system.description: The game its content is for: "nimble", "5e".

any.description: Paths a record has at least one of.

score.description: How sure a match is (0.7 by default). Higher wins when two importers fit.

match.description: A pattern for the links it reads.

data.description: The https address of the data. "{url}" is the link.

license.description: The licence its content comes under, shown before it's imported.

each.description: Where the records are, from the top of the file: "results[*]". Leave it out when the file is one record, or a list of them.

when.description: Only records where this path has a value (or equals this).

into.description: content (a monster, spell…; the default) or note (an NPC, a place…).

kind.description: What each record becomes, as text: "monster", "spell", "npc"… Or { "path": … } to read it from the record.

fields.description: Our fields (the game's content-pack fields, or a note's properties), each from the file.

from.description: Where each record came from. "id" lets a later import update it.

card.description: Notes: the NPC card (look, wants, voice, secret).

records.description: Several sets of records; else this mapping's own each, kind and fields.

card.description: Notes: the NPC card (look, wants, voice, secret).

field.description: A path ("hit_points", "a.b[0]", "a[*]", "a | b"), or a rule.

template.description: Text with {path} slots; {$} is the value at "path".

map.description: The value (any case) to ours; "*" for the rest.
